reviewNotes: HOLD. Lyca Mobile US currently states that the SIM and assigned number expire after 60 days of non-use. Current long-term offers include USD 108/12 months for the 8 GB plan, so the legacy USD 120/year minimum is not retained as a minimum. Exact PAYG keep-alive economics remain unresolved. Current provider and community evidence place new service on AT&T, while 2026 community reports document migration/service problems.

events.outcome: Current official terms retain the 60-day non-use expiry. A current 12-month 8 GB plan is USD 108, so the old USD 120/year claim is not a valid minimum-retention fact; exact PAYG keep-alive cost remains unresolved.
Independent 2026 reports confirm the AT&T migration and include service/account/SIM-swap failures during transition. These are incident evidence, not a route-wide failure rate.

data.acquisitionSummary: Lyca Mobile US sells physical SIM and eSIM prepaid service. Current official 2026 material identifies AT&T coverage; a current long-term 8 GB plan is USD 108 for 12 months.

keep.action: Official plan terms say the SIM and assigned number expire after 60 days of non-use. Use within that interval is required; exact minimum PAYG/top-up action cost is not established in current evidence.

data.chinaActivation: Current eSIM material does not establish a reliable China-first activation path. Earlier VPN/address workaround claims are not promoted without current independent reproduction.
data.kyc: Current Lyca material markets prepaid service without credit checks; identity requirements for every path are not established here.
data.payment: A valid payment method is required; foreign-card/crypto-funded-card reliability is not promoted as verified.
data.roamingSms: The current long-term offer includes USD 5 roaming credit, but China-specific incoming-SMS behavior and minimum roaming-credit mechanics are unresolved.
data.refund: Prepaid plans are described as non-refundable in current plan terms.
data.holdReason: The 60-day non-use clock is current, but the exact lowest-cost keep-alive action and China-first activation/roaming path remain unresolved. 2026 AT&T migration incidents also lower operational confidence.
data.tariffSummary: 60-day non-use expiry is current. USD 108/12-month 8 GB plan is current, but it is not treated as the minimum keep-alive cost.
guideSteps: Do not use the old USD 120/year figure as a minimum-retention rule.
Keep activity inside the official 60-day non-use window.
Treat overseas activation and China SMS behavior as unresolved until reproduced.
